# Why laboratories disagree: an audit of the lever table

*Generated by `scripts/generators/build_lever_disagreement_audit.py` (STATUS_AND_PLAN sec. 0, step 5b). A diagnostic on the keyed literature contrasts; no engine output. Exploratory: the rules were fixed in the generator before its first run, but after the lever table had been read.*

2834 effects (one per numeric contrast, one per pair of levels of a categorical contrast) from 31 laboratories; 99 cells hold two or more laboratories, 15 hold three or more. A cell here is an odorant x lever x band, or an odorant x pair of levels. A pair cell 'B vs A' holds log10(B / A).

## 1. What kind of disagreement each cell shows

| class | cells with 2+ laboratories | cells with 3+ |
|---|---|---|
| conflict between laboratories | 9 | 0 |
| sign changes inside one laboratory | 8 | 3 |
| direction agreed | 55 | 6 |
| no clear effect | 27 | 6 |

Rules, first match: **conflict** = two laboratories' mean effects have opposite signs, each more than 2 standard errors from zero; **sign changes inside one laboratory** = one laboratory has contrasts of both signs, each separable from zero (the effect depends on that study's other settings); **direction agreed** = every laboratory's mean has the same sign; **no clear effect** = mixed signs, none separable from zero. Each contrast's SD is floored at 0.1 dex.

| lever | cells | conflict | sign changes inside a lab | direction agreed | no clear effect |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| amino acid identity | 23 | 1 | 0 | 17 | 5 |
| oxygen | 1 | 0 | 0 | 1 | 0 |
| pH | 15 | 2 | 2 | 8 | 3 |
| precursor dose | 25 | 2 | 2 | 6 | 15 |
| sugar identity | 11 | 4 | 1 | 4 | 2 |
| sulfur source | 5 | 0 | 0 | 4 | 1 |
| temperature | 4 | 0 | 1 | 3 | 0 |
| time | 15 | 0 | 2 | 12 | 1 |

## 3. Which recorded conditions go with disagreement

For pairs of effects in one cell from two different laboratories: the mean |difference| of the pairs that DIFFER on a condition minus that of the pairs that MATCH on it, inside each cell, averaged over cells. A positive gap means that matching on the condition goes with closer agreement. Interval: bootstrap over laboratories.

| condition | gap, dex (90 % interval) | P(gap > 0) | median, matching pairs | median, differing pairs | cells | pairs (match / differ) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| quantification | +0.17 (-0.15 to +0.42) | 0.80 | 0.10 | 0.28 | 7 | 54 / 104 |
| matrix | +0.05 (-0.92 to +0.35) | 0.60 | 0.17 | 0.31 | 8 | 37 / 152 |
| buffered | +0.09 (-0.05 to +0.26) | 0.90 | 0.16 | 0.27 | 15 | 92 / 177 |
| ph_basis | -0.05 (-) | - | 0.66 | 0.70 | 1 | 2 / 6 |
| digitised | -0.06 (-0.22 to +0.12) | 0.46 | 0.30 | 0.27 | 10 | 234 / 166 |
| temperature within 10 C | -0.16 (-0.44 to +0.02) | 0.07 | 0.22 | 0.17 | 17 | 116 / 214 |
| time within 2x | -0.62 (-1.77 to +0.36) | 0.29 | 0.47 | 0.25 | 9 | 220 / 79 |
| pH within 0.5 | +0.07 (-0.10 to +0.32) | 0.68 | 0.38 | 0.20 | 9 | 62 / 115 |
| lever midpoint within 1 step | +0.10 (-0.15 to +0.32) | 0.91 | 0.11 | 0.21 | 8 | 75 / 119 |

**What a laboratory itself is worth.** Pairs from two laboratories differ by +0.13 dex more than pairs from one laboratory in the same cell (+0.05 to +0.33; median 0.14 within a laboratory, 0.23 between; 68 cells).

### 3b. The SIZE of agreed effects (55 cells whose laboratories agree in direction)

Same method, but the distance between two same-sign effects is |log10 of their size ratio| (effects of at least 0.05 dex). A positive gap: laboratories that match on the condition agree more closely on size.

| condition | gap, dex (90 % interval) | P(gap > 0) | median, matching | median, differing | cells | pairs (match / differ) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|

| matrix | +0.00 (-0.70 to +0.29) | 0.43 | 0.35 | 0.65 | 3 | 6 / 42 |

| time within 2x | -0.02 (-0.32 to +0.21) | 0.50 | 0.24 | 0.53 | 7 | 104 / 50 |
| pH within 0.5 | -0.07 (-0.37 to +0.37) | 0.50 | 0.63 | 0.24 | 5 | 46 / 57 |

Two effects from one laboratory differ in size by a median factor 1.4; from two laboratories, 1.6 (gap +0.08 dex, +0.01 to +0.29).

## What this cannot say

- The conditions are those the papers print and the keying recorded. The true pH during heating, the extraction recovery, free against bound thiol and the headspace are mostly not recorded, so they cannot be tested here.
- Conditions travel together: a laboratory that uses peak areas also tends to use a food matrix. A gap is an association inside cells, not a cause.
- Pairs share laboratories, so the bootstrap resamples laboratories; with few laboratories per cell the intervals are wide and a null result is weak evidence of no effect.
